chunks: The right of the elder is that you show him reverence because of his age, and honor him because he entered Islam before you, and refrain from confronting him in a dispute, and do not precede him in a path, nor go ahead of him, and do not consider him foolish; and if he acts foolishly toward you, you bear with him and honor him because of the right of Islam and its sanctity.

key_terms.الْكَبِيرِ: The elder (one who is older in age or seniority)
key_terms.لِحَقِّ الْإِسْلَامِ: Because of the right of Islam

ai.seo_question: What are the specific etiquettes and rights of elders in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin expands the concept of elder respect beyond mere age to include precedence in Islam, prescribing specific behavioral etiquette such as yielding the path and avoiding argumentative confrontation. This guidance reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a manifestation of *haqq* (right), where honoring the elder is ultimately an act of honoring the sanctity of Islam itself.
